I built [gemnotes](https://github.com/dylanpieper/gemnotes) for my wife, Julia ❤️, so she could track her hours toward clinical licensure. The process is arduous: therapists have to log thousands of hours across categories like individual and relational sessions, supervision, and administrative work before they can practice independently. gemnotes is a multi-user Shiny app that tracks all of it.

![](/media/gemnotes-dash.png){fig-alt="gemnotes dashboard showing licensure hour tracking" fig-align="center" width="700"}

## Private by Design

Every therapist signs in with their Google account and gets a private dashboard. All accounts share the same Postgres tables, but row-level security scopes every query to the signed-in user's own rows, so no one can read or write another therapist's hours. Sign-in works off the Google ID token directly, without a server-side OAuth exchange. Each user sets their own goals for total hours, therapy hours, relational hours, and supervision hours in a signup wizard, and can delete their account and data at any time.

If you're a therapist tracking hours toward licensure, you can use the app yourself at [gemnotes](https://dylanpieper-gemnotes.share.connect.posit.cloud/). This is the most important app I've built, because it's for the most important person in my life. Building her tools is one of my love languages.
